pr_title: Implement legacy hit explosions for osu!catch
pr_body:
Closes #12095

- [x] Depends on #8019.

Implements hit explosions for legacy skins that closely matches stable's hit explosions.

Comparison video:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4877041/113530354-70c6c680-958b-11eb-8408-8853bb2684a1.mp4

(The hyperfuit objects being incorrect is not relevant to this PR)
The stable catch players I've shown this to are happy with its similarity with stable, and it accomplishes what was asked in the issue. 


Improves pooling logic for catch hit explosions.


Hit explosions for default and legacy currently are not created when the hit object is a Droplet.
pr_comments:
That looks so much better now.

One thing that confuses me is does the hit explosion length matches in stable version because of that video?
The calculations are the same as stable. The difference can be explained by the difference of the Y position of the catcher.
Can i ask if its intentional that only the classic skin get the hit explosion and not the custom legacy skins?

@amberkowalski I was going to look at bringing this one up-to-date, but the merge conflict here is quite complicated. The underlying container which you were modifying has since been updated, to the point it *may* be better to apply your changes again to `master` rather than attempt to get this PR up-to-date.

Are you able to take a look into this? The dependency is almost ready to go, so I think this has a good chance of getting merged in the coming days/weeks.

Sure, just so we're clear 

> apply your changes again to master 

my thought seeing this is to check out master, then apply all the changes I made in this PR to master manually then rebase and force push. I just want to check since you might mean something else or I might be going about it wrong. Thanks!

The optimal path is to merge `master` into this branch, but as you'll see it's a bit of a mess.

If you're going to apply changes to `master` please open a new PR rather than force pushing (and reference/close this one).
As a heads up I've put some work into updating this PR with latest `master` but I still have a few things to check before it's PRable.

issue_context.title: Add a vertical hit lighting effect after catching a fruit
issue_context.body:
Stable not only uses a short horizontal hit lighting effect in the place but also a vertical hit lighting effect making sure that you've catched a fruit while looking at the middle of the screen and not to stare into the catcher.

The reason why it's important to have a vertical hit lighting effect because you can easily play the map without looking down the monitor. The only way you can look at the fruit without looking to anything is the combo number. With this added effect the gameplay in lazer would be much more visible while playing.

Stable hit lighting in full effect (with enabled full screen and 1920x1080):
![](https://puu.sh/HqPaP/c93f6c5846.png)
comments: In stable I don't like how this effect obscures/blends with the falling fruit, and is the main reason why I do not enjoy playing the osu!catch gamemode.

Unfortunately the majority of players I've talked with during the Season Spotlight said that the current hit lighting feels nonexistent and said that it feels like you've been playing without them.

I didn't mentioned it should be reached to the top of the window but if that's your main critique then it could be cut in half above the combo number? At least being one of the options on how this could be implemented in the first place.

Any implementation of this should ensure that the hit lighting can be turned off via the "Hit lighting" setting option. As it'll also be skinnable, I imagine users will also be able to provide their own texture if they want a different one.

Agree on the skinnable part. Originally you could technically turn it off in stable by changing the hit lighting to black with the 100% background dim and it would feel like you're playing without them in lazer. Right now it wasn't implemented and there's no current answer that it'll be featured or not.

I'm interested in implementing this, however this requires design work(?). I don't mind copying stable or working from some sort of concept image / drawing, however I understand if its just easier for someone who knows what you guys want it to look like to implement it.

I do not believe design work is necessary here. I believe the current hit explosion still should be used on the lazer default skin, and the stable explosion sprite should be used for the stable/legacy default skin.
Is it already skinnable? I thought I got the lazer effect on both classic and lazer skin.

[It is not skinnable.](https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/master/osu.Game.Rulesets.Catch/UI/HitExplosion.cs) It should be, the same way numerous other skin elements are. I guess for completion's sake you would also need details of how the explosion sprite animates on stable.

Note that the current implementation already uses object pooling, so it may not be very easy to get this working completely correctly if you're not very familiar with what pooling is or how it is done.
That's what I thought I saw, I just got confused for a second. I'll see what I can do, thank you for the info!

We do have a design in mind for the default skin, so if implementing this I would do it for classic skin only for now (or keep that in mind when implementing and use the standard separation flow, leaving the default empty or copying the effect from osu!mania as a placeholder).

I've kept the lazer hit lighting effect the exact same as it was before, and implemented support for having the legacy version of the hit lighting effect. How should I go about actually implementing the legacy effect? Is there a sprite somewhere with animation information that I'd need?

The current implementation creates hit lighting on droplets, is this something that you'd like preserved? Additionally, is that something that would make sense to be a skin setting? AFAIK the current osu skin.ini doesn't support setting that, so for legacy skins it would probably be forced to `false`? Sorry if I'm misjudging functionality, I'm still learning how everything fits together

It should behave how it does in stable, so droplets would need to be excluded I think. Probably passed in as a parameter so we can potentially allow customisation in the future of skinning. Shouldn't be exposing any new user-facing settings just yet though.
Sounds good, I think for now I can just pass the `PalpableCatchHitObject` into the explosion as a reasonable solution for now.

I'm curious as to how CS scaling is applied to the explosion sprites in stable. I'm currently having an issue where on low CS maps the explosions don't constrain themselves to the platter. As far as I can tell, the math code should be the same so I'm suspecting there's a difference in how the scaling is applied to the explosion sprites in stable.

[Code Here](https://gist.github.com/amberkowalski/e20ff32f7029f334f663ee67c91cbe28)

Video:
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4877041/113493365-477f3b00-94a4-11eb-94db-2f313e02756e.mp4
Can you link a pushed branch to check out or something? Easier to just look at that than to guess at a gist.
[Here you go!](https://github.com/amberkowalski/osu/tree/ctb-hitlighting). Sorry about that, when I made the comment I wasn't in a nice spot to push it, I should have updated it with a link.

I believe the clamping is not working as intended because of a conflation of slightly different constants. Stable defines

```csharp
catchMargin = catcherWidth * 0.1f;
```

while you have

```csharp
hitExplosion.CatcherMargin = ALLOWED_CATCH_RANGE; // is 0.8
```

You could see how those are *kinda* the same constant (stable's is measured as the margin from edges, while on your branch it's the width of the catching area), but due to that difference no actual clamping is taking place. I believe you'd want something like the following:

```csharp
hitExplosion.CatcherMargin = (1 - ALLOWED_CATCH_RANGE) / 2;
```

Just wanted to check, are we looking for an exact perfect reproduction or stable or "looks pretty much like stable". I've got it looking like stable and it accomplishes what was requested from the issue. I've also consulted some ctb players and they also think it looks okay.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4877041/113507058-e3915c80-950d-11eb-86f6-578c59b5ccd2.mp4

If this looks okay, I will open a PR. If there are any obvious flaws, I will fix them beforehand.

Obviously the closer the better, but it looks mostly like it should it's probably fine to PR.

What I can say for sure is that the PR should come with a visual test (so that the animation can be examined better). A visual comparison against stable would also be appreciated. If you are able to put together a video of a map with a juice stream down the middle and splice it such that one side shows stable and the other shows lazer (so that possible discrepancies can be seen at the seam between the halves), it would definitely go a long way.
That's a good idea, I'll get that put together, fix anything horribly wrong if I see it, and make the final preparations for a PR.

Here's how it looks so far, going to hold off on the PR and tune the vertical scale and opacity a little more, otherwise looks okay. The platter appears to be at a different height, but that wasn't changed by me so I'm not planning on addressing it.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4877041/113508240-792fea80-9514-11eb-9dd7-c47f54d4c163.mp4
The catcher height difference will probably be more in scope of #12079.

review_comments: This check should be based on the presence of a catcher sprite, not the explosion sprite directly. This particular texture is actually not skinnable in `osu-stable` (and we don't want to introduce no skinnable scope where it wasn't there previously) and should always use the default legacy skin implementation.

As above, these should come from the default legacy skin, rather than the user's skin. I'm not 100% sure we have a method of doing this yet, so may require a bit of further investigation. There's an issue open for the more general case (#8019) but this is an explicit "do not want" case, which is a bit different.

Out of curiosity, does this even work right now? No catch skin should include this sprite as it won't actually apply on osu-stable.

> Out of curiosity, does this even work right now? No catch skin should include this sprite as it won't actually apply on osu-stable.

You're right about that, I've only been testing with the "classic" skin so it did have the files. I'll take a look at getting it to work as required, then.
Unfortunately this might not be an easy one, and may need a solution to #8019 as a prerequisite, but see how you go.

Is there a reason this is done with a fixed duration here? I guess this was just copied from mania's implementation?

Wondering if we can potentially use the expiry of the nested skinnable here..

I can't find a good way to accomplish that, although I agree it should be done. As far as I can tell, there's no method that I can override in `CatchHitExplosion` to accomplish this locally. Provided that I am correct, would adding `OnExpire` or `OnDied` to `Drawable` be something we could do, then hook into it in the pool?
